{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Remove QA rows first
qa_mask = df['revenue'] == '999,999.99'
df_clean = df[~qa_mask].copy()

# Clean revenue: remove commas and convert to float
# Even though no commas were found in the remaining data,
# do it safely to handle any potential Excel formatting
if df_clean['revenue'].str.contains(',', na=False).any():
    df_clean['revenue_clean'] = df_clean['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)
else:
    df_clean['revenue_clean'] = df_clean['revenue'].astype(float)

# Now check channel and customer_segment distribution
# The data dictionary says channel was not randomized: email campaign targeted loyal customers
# So we must check if the groups are comparable
print("Channel distribution across customer segments:")
print(pd.crosstab(df_clean['channel'], df_clean['customer_segment']))

# Check if the QA rows were distributed unevenly across channels
print("\nQA rows by channel:")
print(df.loc[qa_mask, 'channel'].value_counts())"}
